basic_info.item_name: Squadra Corse Driverless PoliTO (Politecnico di Torino)
basic_info.competition_series: FSAE Italy (primary), FS Germany (FSG), FS Austria (FSA), FS Spain, FS Portugal, FS Czech - broad multi-event European circuit
basic_info.summary: Squadra Corse PoliTo was founded in winter 2004 by ten students and switched to an electric powertrain in 2012, becoming the first Italian FS team to do so. Driverless-specific engineering began as academic thesis work inside the main team around 2018-2019 - two DIMEAS Master's theses (Emergency Brake System and an electromechanical steering actuator) were both built for the SC19 car ('Lucia') during the 2018-2019 academic year, timed to FSG's 2017 introduction of the Driverless class. A dedicated 'Squadra Corse DRIVERLESS' subteam was then founded in 2020, inheriting the SC19 prototype, and was formally announced by Politecnico di Torino in March 2021. First confirmed competition podium-adjacent driverless result came with the 'VaLentina' car at Formula Student Italy 2022 (3rd place, Driverless category). Since then, results have been mixed and often incomplete (several seasons show 'DV Sportability: not competed'), and the team's own 2026 SC26 car is explicitly described as marking the 'debut of autonomous driving' - implying that, roughly six years after the dedicated subteam was founded, the 2026 season is still positioned as the first time the team reliably completes autonomous dynamic running. The team also built a structured 'SC Academy' mentoring program specifically to counter annual student turnover.

history.dv_program_start: Approximately 2018 (academic year 2018-2019), when the first DIMEAS Master's theses on the Emergency Brake System and the autonomous steering actuator began, both explicitly scoped for converting the SC19 car ('Lucia') into a Driverless Vehicle. A dedicated Driverless subteam was later founded in 2020 (inheriting the SC19 prototype) and formally publicly announced by Politecnico di Torino on 9 March 2021.

history.ramp_phases: Named/inferable phases: (1) 'Thesis-driven R&D inside the main team' (2018-2019) - EBS and steering actuator designed as academic Master's theses for the shared SC19 car; (2) 'Dedicated subteam, inherited chassis' (2020-2021) - Squadra Corse DRIVERLESS founded and publicly established, reusing the existing SC19 prototype rather than a purpose-built DV chassis; (3) 'First competitive results' (2022) - VaLentina places in the Driverless category and scores DV Sportability/Acceleration points; (4) 'Inconsistent dynamic completion' (2024-2025) - several seasons show DV Sportability as 'not competed'; (5) 'Reliability & true autonomous debut' (2026) - SC26 explicitly framed by the team as the actual debut of autonomous driving.
history.what_slipped: The most striking, well-evidenced slip is organizational-to-competitive lag: the dedicated Driverless subteam was founded in 2020 and formally announced in March 2021, yet the team's own SC26 (2026) car is explicitly marketed as the 'debut of autonomous driving' - roughly five to six years after subteam formation, and about eight years after the first DV-specific theses (2018). Multiple competition seasons in between (2024, 2025) show 'DV Sportability: not competed' in the official results database, indicating repeated failures to complete driverless dynamic events even after entering the class and scoring static/design points. This points to a chronic gap between design/inspection readiness and reliable on-track autonomous performance, not a one-time schedule miss.
history.platform_prerequisites: Yes, but PoliTo retrofitted rather than co-designed: the team had 8 years of electric-powertrain experience (2012-2020) before founding a dedicated Driverless subteam, but the DV subteam inherited the existing SC19 chassis (originally developed as a driver-operated electric car, per the EBS thesis noting SC19 was developed 'predominantly...as a car with driver') rather than building a DV-native platform. This retrofit approach required fitting the EBS actuator into the constrained existing cockpit/pedal-box space and modifying the pedal box and steering rack to accommodate autonomous actuators.

technical_features.ebs_design: Hydro-pneumatic Emergency Brake System (SC19, AY2018-2019 thesis, Mohammed Zubair Ahmed): a hydraulic actuator is driven by a hydro-pneumatic intensifier, controlled via solenoid-actuated (two-position, three-way) valves, fed from a pressure-regulated high-pressure gas canister. The hydraulic actuator, mounted behind the brake pedal, pulls the pedal to imitate manual braking, exploiting the car's existing hydraulic service brakes rather than adding a separate brake circuit. Sized for a 1550N pull force in the pull-load condition; actuator design pressure up to 300 bar. Designed as a passive system with mechanically stored energy to satisfy FS2020 rulebook DV3.1.3. Primary autonomous-mode braking is instead handled by a separate 'brake-by-wire' system - the EBS is emergency-only.
technical_features.ebs_development_duration: 1 academic year (2018-2019) as a DIMEAS Master's thesis (Automotive Engineering)
technical_features.steering_actuation: Electromechanical steering actuator (SC19/'Lucia', AY2018-2019 thesis, Sarath Babu Nagarajan): a BLDC motor coupled to a planetary gearbox, rigidly coupled to a ball screw shaft over which a ball nut is engaged, converting rotary motion to linear motion; a transfer unit connects the ball nut to an actuator link, which connects via clevises to the steering tie rods and turns the front wheels. The steering rack itself is a custom rack-and-pinion design with a herringbone-like gear profile, redesigned in 'Lucia' (SC19) to cut approximately 7.5kg of weight versus the previous car. A conceptual Design FMEA (severity/occurrence/detection scales) was performed on the Autonomous Steering System. Specific DT.2.2 mechanical decoupling detail (for returning to manual steering) was not confirmed in accessible excerpts.
technical_features.brake_actuation: 'Brake-by-wire' system used for primary/normal-mode autonomous braking, kept distinct from the passive hydro-pneumatic EBS reserved for emergency stops.
technical_features.sensor_mounting_packaging: [uncertain] Not found in detail in accessible sources beyond the EBS actuator being fitted 'behind the brake pedal' within the existing (non-DV-native) cockpit and pedal-box, requiring pedal-box base-plate modification.
technical_features.mass_added: Partial data point only: the redesigned steering rack in SC19/'Lucia' saved approximately 7.5kg versus the prior car's steering system (a mass reduction, not the total DV system mass added). Total driverless-system mass added was not found in accessible sources.
technical_features.chassis_impact: Brake pedal and pedal-box base plate modified to accommodate the EBS hydraulic actuator, with FEA (CATIA design, Altair Hyperworks stress analysis) performed to verify safe stress limits; steering rack redesigned as part of the DV conversion.
technical_features.compute_platform: SC26 (2026): NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Earlier-generation compute platform (2020-2022 era) not confirmed in accessible sources.
technical_features.sensor_suite: AY2020-2021 (Global Mapping thesis): ZED stereo camera + Velodyne LiDAR for the perception pipeline, SBG Ellipse-N inertial navigation system (INS) for localization. 'VaLentina' (2022): described generically as 'Lidar, Stereocamera and INS IMU.' SC26 (2026): dual cameras + Ouster LiDAR (an upgrade from the earlier Velodyne unit).
technical_features.custom_pcbs: [uncertain] The team's public GitHub org includes general electronics/firmware repos (fenice-bms-lv - Battery Management System Low Voltage board firmware; dash - dashboard board; openblt_enzommino - CAN bootloader) but these appear to cover the main Squadra Corse electric powertrain rather than DV-specific autonomy hardware; no DV-specific custom PCB design/fab/bring-up duration was found.
technical_features.software_stack: ROS1-based (per the AY2020-2021 Global Mapping thesis, which explicitly documents Catkin build system, ROS Master/node/topic architecture, Rostest, and Rosbash tooling), with the autonomous system 'tested and experimentally validated both with simulations in ROS and' (physical testing, per thesis excerpt). EKF-based state estimation is documented (thesis appendix: 'EKF Parameters Configuration').
technical_features.ros_version: ROS1 as of the AY2020-2021 Global Mapping thesis (Catkin-based); [uncertain] whether the team has since migrated to ROS2
technical_features.perception_approach: ZED stereo camera + Velodyne LiDAR fusion for cone detection and environment perception (AY2020-2021 thesis); later cars use an upgraded dual-camera + Ouster LiDAR suite (SC26, 2026). Specific detection algorithm (CNN/YOLO variant vs. classical clustering) was not confirmed in accessible sources.
technical_features.slam_localization_approach: SBG Ellipse-N INS plus an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for state estimation, combined with a dedicated 'Global Mapping Algorithm' (Emanuele Bertrand, AY2020-2021 Master's thesis) providing the SLAM/mapping representation for the driverless race car. A follow-on thesis ('State Estimation for Formula Student Driverless Application,' Davide Leonetti, AY2023-2024) extended this by estimating longitudinal and lateral velocity in the absence of a dedicated Ground Speed Sensor, explicitly to improve position-mapping accuracy beyond what GPS alone provides.
technical_features.control_approach: [uncertain] Described only qualitatively - the SC22 vehicle is noted as having a 'significantly more advanced control system' than prior cars; no specific method (pure pursuit/Stanley/MPC) was confirmed in accessible sources.
technical_features.simulation_tooling: ROS-based simulation used to validate the autonomous system prior to physical testing, per the AY2020-2021 Global Mapping thesis ('tested and experimentally validated both with simulations in ROS and [real-world testing]'). Specific simulator name (e.g. Gazebo/custom) not confirmed.
technical_features.open_source_repos: github.com/squadracorsedriverless (7 public repos): tsal (software-defined TSAL), dash (dashboard board firmware), fenice-bms-lv (forked Battery Management System - Low Voltage), carrell.ino and openblt_enzommino (charging-cart/CAN-bootloader firmware), stoppa, and SC19-sensor (archived, marked 'Rest in Peace'). These repos are predominantly embedded/firmware-focused rather than perception/SLAM/planning code, making them a weak reference for the autonomy software stack. The team's public Master's theses hosted on webthesis.biblio.polito.it (EBS, steering actuator, global mapping/SLAM, state estimation, autonomous control systems) are a substantially better and more detailed public reference than the GitHub org for this team.

milestone_significance.critical_path_items: 1) The EBS design and its FS2020 DV3.1.3 passive-system requirement - a full academic-year thesis (AY2018-2019) was needed to design a hydro-pneumatic actuator that could be retrofitted into the SC19 cockpit's tight packaging envelope. 2) The steering actuator's mechanical integration and FMEA - also a full academic-year thesis, requiring a custom rack redesign to fit the electromechanical actuator while cutting weight (7.5kg saved). 3) The organizational transition from thesis-driven R&D embedded in the main ICE/EV team to a dedicated Driverless subteam (2020, publicly announced March 2021) - this organizational restructuring, rather than any single piece of hardware, appears to be the largest gating factor, given that the team itself still describes 2026 (SC26) as the 'debut of autonomous driving' roughly five to six years later.
milestone_significance.long_lead_procurement: [uncertain] No numeric lead times (in weeks) were disclosed in accessible sources for the Velodyne/Ouster LiDAR, SBG Ellipse-N INS, or Jetson AGX Orin compute hardware.
milestone_significance.first_dynamic_test_date: [uncertain] Not found in accessible sources; earliest confirmed dynamic/competition result is 2022 (VaLentina)
milestone_significance.validation_strategy: FEA-based structural validation (CATIA design plus Altair Hyperworks stress analysis, and an Excel-based brake-force calculator) for the EBS actuator and modified pedal box; a conceptual Design FMEA (severity/occurrence/detection scoring) performed for the Autonomous Steering System; ROS-based simulation used to validate the autonomous software stack before physical/on-vehicle testing, per the AY2020-2021 Global Mapping thesis. No description of a formal whole-vehicle validation program (e.g. required test-track hours, EBS pass/fail test log) was found in accessible sources.

competition_ecosystem.rules_compliance_challenges: Designing the EBS as a passive system with mechanically stored energy (FS2020 rule DV3.1.3) while retrofitting it into a cockpit and brake-pedal assembly not originally designed for a DV actuator was explicitly the central engineering challenge of the 2018-2019 EBS thesis. The steering actuator's FMEA work references DV2.2.6-related driver/actuator interaction constraints when estimating pedal/actuator forces. More broadly, retrofitting DV hardware onto an existing ICE/EV-lineage chassis (SC19) rather than a purpose-built DV chassis appears to have made packaging and integration (not the control algorithms) the harder rules-compliance problem, per the theses' repeated emphasis on space constraints.

performance_metrics.dv_event_results: FS Italy 2022: VaLentina, 3rd place Driverless category. FS Austria 2022: 15th overall/25 teams, 16th DV Sportability, 4th DV Acceleration. FSAE Italy 2022: 5th overall/26 teams, 2nd DV Sportability, 7th DV Acceleration. FS Germany 2022: 50th overall/63 teams, DV Sportability not competed. FSAE Italy 2024: 13th overall/34 teams, 11th DV Sportability. FS Germany 2024: 48th overall/79 teams, 21st DV Sportability. FS Austria 2024: 28th overall/38 teams, DV Sportability not competed. FSAE Italy 2025: 25th overall/32 teams, DV Sportability not competed. FS Spain 2025: 16th overall/37 teams, DV Sportability not competed. FS Germany 2026: 30th overall/80 teams, 28th DV Sportability. FS Portugal 2026: 3rd overall/12 teams, DV Sportability not competed. (Source: formulastudent.de team results database.)
performance_metrics.reliability_notes: 'DV Sportability: not competed' recurs across multiple official results (2022 FS Germany, 2024 FS Austria, 2025 FSAE Italy, 2025 FS Spain, 2026 FS Portugal), indicating repeated failures to complete the Driverless dynamic events even in seasons where the car scored static/design or overall points. The team's own description of SC26 (2026) as the 'debut of autonomous driving' - years after the subteam's 2020-2021 founding and after multiple prior competition seasons - is itself the strongest available signal of a chronic reliability/readiness gap between entering the DV class and completing autonomous dynamic runs.

top_mistakes: [uncertain] Not directly stated by the team in accessible sources. Inferred from the record: retrofitting the DV system onto SC19, a chassis originally developed 'predominantly as a car with driver' (per the EBS thesis), created cockpit/packaging constraints that both major mechanical theses (EBS, steering) had to design around, rather than being freed to co-design the vehicle for autonomy from the start. The repeated 'DV Sportability: not competed' results across 2022-2026, combined with the team's own 2026 'debut of autonomous driving' framing, suggest that organizational/staffing continuity (not a single technical blocker) was the dominant constraint on turning design-stage DV work into consistently completed on-track autonomous runs.
advice_for_new_teams: [uncertain] No direct quotes from Squadra Corse Driverless PoliTo were found in accessible sources. The team's creation of a structured 'SC Academy' mentoring program - explicitly built to 'train new members, mitigate annual turnover, and secure the seamless transfer of know-how,' reportedly with PhD-level mentoring support - is the closest available evidence of the team's own institutional view that turnover/knowledge-transfer, not raw engineering difficulty, was their biggest recurring obstacle.
team_structure_dv: Squadra Corse DRIVERLESS operates as a subteam distinct from the main (ICE/EV) Squadra Corse team, founded in 2020 and formally announced 9 March 2021. As of the 2026 team bio, the subteam comprises approximately 30 students across ten engineering disciplines and twelve nationalities. A 'Perception & Planning' (P&P) division is referenced in a 2020-2021 Master's thesis acknowledgment. The team runs a structured onboarding program, 'SC Academy,' with PhD-level mentoring support, specifically to train new members and transfer institutional knowledge given annual student turnover.
recruiting_and_knowledge_transfer: The team's 'SC Academy' program is explicitly designed to 'train new members, mitigate annual turnover, and secure the seamless transfer of know-how,' with structured mentoring involving PhD students - a direct, named institutional response to the chronic Formula Student turnover problem. No further quantitative detail (program duration, cohort size) was found in accessible sources.
budget_estimate: [uncertain] Not disclosed in accessible sources; the team is sponsored/supported by Politecnico di Torino's CARS interdepartmental center and by industry partners including Italdesign, per the founding announcement and Italdesign co-branded materials.
recommended_sequence: Inferred from Squadra Corse's own build order: (1) build EV competency first at the main-team level (PoliTo had 8 years of electric-powertrain experience, 2012-2020, before dedicating a subteam to driverless); (2) run early DV subsystem design as funded/supervised academic thesis projects (PoliTo used DIMEAS Master's theses for both the EBS and the steering actuator, getting a full academic year of dedicated, documented, professor-supervised engineering per subsystem before committing broader team resources); (3) only spin up a dedicated DV subteam once core safety-critical subsystems (EBS, steering actuator) are proven on paper via FMEA/FEA; (4) invest in a structured onboarding/mentoring program (SC Academy) early, rather than after turnover has already caused repeated 'not competed' dynamic-event results, since PoliTo's own multi-year gap between subteam founding (2020) and its self-described 'debut of autonomous driving' (2026) suggests the mentoring program came later than it should have.
applicability_to_24_month_ramp: Squadra Corse's own history argues against replicating their approach on a 24-month timeline: from the first DV-specific theses (2018) to the dedicated subteam's founding (2020) to the team's own claimed 'debut of autonomous driving' (SC26, 2026) spans roughly eight years, and even after the subteam formed the results database shows repeated 'DV Sportability: not competed' seasons well into 2025. The clearest transferable lesson for UMSAE, which already has a running EV and does not need PoliTo's multi-year EV-first prerequisite, is to avoid PoliTo's staged 'thesis-project-then-subteam-then-actually-drive' cadence: commit a dedicated, resourced DV team and a DV-appropriate car/chassis plan from day one rather than retrofitting DV hardware onto a chassis designed for a human driver, since PoliTo's own EBS and steering theses both had to design around packaging compromises created by that retrofit approach. A second transferable practice worth copying directly is PoliTo's use of structured academic/thesis-style deliverables (a defined scope, a supervisor, and a hard academic-year deadline) to force real progress on safety-critical subsystems like the EBS and steering actuator - a discipline a 9-person software-focused team could emulate with internal milestone-and-review cadences even without a university-thesis structure. Finally, UMSAE should build (or borrow from PoliTo's SC Academy concept) an explicit knowledge-transfer/onboarding plan from the start of the 24-month window, since PoliTo's own multi-year stall appears at least partly attributable to turnover/institutional-memory loss rather than pure engineering difficulty.
